lines.trans: Welcome to Paris, dear Madame Weaver!
Thank you very much, I am delighted to be here.
Oh, but you speak French very well!
I love speaking French with you.
Andrea has a big nanny problem.
It is not a problem at all.

words.gloss: completely; tout à fait = completely, du tout = at all

lines.trans: She will join us directly at the hotel.
But first, I have a vital appointment.
An appointment with a great director?
No, with the best Parisian pastries!
I want to taste every flavor.
Orange blossom macarons!

words.gloss: orange tree; fleur d'oranger = orange blossom

lines.trans: It is my favorite treat in Paris.
You have truly exquisite tastes.

examples.trans: First of all, let's talk about work.

examples.text: Il y a un macaron sur la table.
examples.trans: There's a macaron on the table.

meanings.note: elle a quarante ans = she is forty

meanings.en: il y a = there is / there are

examples.trans: You know a lot of people.

meanings.en: beaucoup de = a lot of, many

meanings.note: as a masculine noun: pour le bien de = for the good of
la bienvenue = the welcome; also used as greeting
before a noun: ce film, cette tête, ces gens
as a pronoun in c'est, ce n'est pas; becomes c' before a vowel

examples.text: Il est charmant et très attentif.
examples.trans: He is charming and very attentive.

examples.text: J'ai perdu un ami très cher.
examples.trans: I've lost a very dear friend.

meanings.note: before the noun: un ami très cher
after the noun or after être

examples.text: La plus grande imprésario de Paris.
Pourquoi il ne m'appelle pas directement?
examples.trans: Why doesn't he call me directly?

examples.text: Elle est trop vieille pour le rôle.
examples.trans: She's too old for the part.

examples.text: Ces pâtisseries ont un goût exquis.
examples.trans: These pastries have an exquisite taste.

meanings.note: no capital letter for the adjective

examples.text: Les macarons sont une douce gourmandise.

meanings.note: avoir quel goût? = to taste like what?
before the noun: un gros contrat

examples.text: Il avait une chambre à l'hôtel Saint-Georges.
examples.trans: He had a room at the Hotel Saint-Georges.

examples.text: On connaît le patron de l'hôtel.
examples.trans: We know the owner of the hotel.

meanings.note: before the verb: vous la connaissez? les voilà

meanings.en: macaron, a small round almond biscuit

examples.text: Je veux, mais je ne peux pas.
examples.trans: I want to, but I can't.

meanings.note: merci beaucoup = thank you very much
ne ... pas: not; ne ... plus: not anymore; ne ... jamais: never
tag at the end of a question

examples.text: C'est un questionnaire pour la nounou.
examples.trans: This is a questionnaire for the nanny.

examples.text: La nounou arrive à huit heures.
examples.trans: The nanny arrives at eight o'clock.

meanings.en: Parisian, of or relating to the city of Paris
pas du tout: not at all

meanings.note: invariable in plural: un pas, des pas
also used as a noun: mon préféré = my favourite (one)

examples.text: Nous achetons des gâteaux à la pâtisserie.
examples.trans: We buy cakes at the pastry shop.

examples.text: Il a appris que Mathias rejoint StarMédia.
examples.trans: He heard that Mathias is joining StarMédia.

examples.text: Je te rejoins dans cinq minutes.
examples.trans: I'll meet you in five minutes.

rejoindre.gloss: to join, to meet up with

examples.trans: I have an appointment with the doctor.

meanings.note: avoir rendez-vous avec = to have an appointment with

examples.trans: She wants to taste each flavor.
He's a star. / She's a star.
The stars are arriving in Cannes.

meanings.note: always feminine, even for a man: une star

examples.text: Ça ne va pas du tout.

meanings.note: oui à tout = yes to everything
plural tous (pronounced 'tous' with s): merci à tous
before a noun: tout le monde = everyone
+ noun: je veux un café; + infinitive: je veux partir
je vous rappelle = I'll call you back
place: à Paris, à mon cours

meanings.en: au = à + le, aux = à + les
